events.text: Rock Crystal egg created for Empress Alexandra Feodorovna.

evidence.quote: It was created in 1896 for Empress Alexandra Feodorovna

events.text: Presented by Nicholas II to Alexandra Fedorovna.

evidence.quote: The egg was presented by Nicholas II to Alexandra Fedorovna on March 24 , 1896

events.text: Housed in the Empress study in the Winter Palace.

evidence.quote: In 1909 , the egg was housed in the Empress study in the Winter Palace

events.text: Sold by the Antikvariat to Hammer Galleries, New York City.

evidence.quote: In 1930 , the Rock Crystal Egg was one of the ten Eggs sold by the Antikvariat

events.text: Bought by Lillian Thomas Pratt, wife of John Lee Pratt.

evidence.quote: In 1945 the egg became the last of five Imperial Easter Eggs bought by Lillian Thomas Pratt

events.text: Willed to Virginia Museum of Fine Arts after Pratt's death.

evidence.quote: Upon Lillian Thomas Pratts death in 1947 , the egg was willed to Virginia Museum of Fine Arts

undated_mentions: Seized by the Kerensky Provisional Government and moved with about 40 other eggs to the Armory Palace of the Kremlin, Moscow
